logp.method_description: The octanol/water partition coefficient, log P measurement was carried out using an adaptation of the shake-flask method based on a literature method1 and guided by OECD test protocol 107.2 Octanol (10 mL) and either HPLC-grade H2O or phosphate buffered saline (PBS) (for Log P; pH 7.4) were mutually saturated by shaking the biphasic mixture of the two phases overnight at ambient temperature. An aqueous stock of complex solution of known concentration was added to 800 μL octanol to calculate the relative response factor of the complex in octanol. Each complex solution was added to 1.00 mL aqueous phase to a final concentration of 20 μM and shaken with 1.00 mL aqueous saturated octanol for 2 h at 25 °C. The neat phases were partitioned and each sample analysed inS3triplicate by UV-vis absorption spectroscopy to determine the concentration in each layer and the LogP calculated according to equation (1). At pH 7.4, Log P = Log D for non-ionisable compounds. Log Po/w = log([Ru]octanol / [Ru]water)
